claims: President Donald Trump fired U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
Pam Bondi had a 14-month tenure as U.S. Attorney General.
According to reports, Bondi faced mounting criticism and internal scrutiny over her management of the Department of Justice's release of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Trump was reportedly unhappy that Bondi had not acted aggressively enough to investigate or prosecute his political adversaries such as former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James.
Critics argued her term was defined by attempting to turn the DOJ into a tool for political vendettas.
Critics argued she failed to meet the high demands of the White House to secure convictions against critics.
Key outside advisors to Trump, such as Boris Epshteyn and federal housing official Bill Pulte, reportedly pushed for her removal.
Boris Epshteyn and Bill Pulte blamed her for "slow-walking" cases against political enemies.
